title: Touch control fault
shortDescription: A touch key appears permanently pressed on the glass control.
fullDescription:
Error E1 on a Bosch induction or ceramic cooktop means the control detects a key held for more than 10 seconds at startup. Spilled liquid, metal utensils, or a wet cloth left on the control area are the usual causes.

The cooktop locks out until the surface is clear and dry.

causes.cause: Liquid or object on touch area

fixSteps.title: Clean surface
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the glass completely dry and make sure nothing covers the touch strip.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Flip the cooktop breaker off for 5 minutes, then on.

fixSteps.title: Replace touch module
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists with a clean dry glass, replace the touch control module.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you are not confident lifting the glass; induction cooktops use heavy tempered glass.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch cooktop E1 touch control fix

faq.q: Why does this happen so often?
faq.a: Boil-overs onto the touch strip are the main cause.

title: Zone over-temperature
shortDescription: A cooking zone reached a protective temperature limit.
fullDescription:
E2 means a zone's temperature sensor reports the glass or induction coil is too hot. Bosch shuts that zone down to prevent damage to the glass and electronics.

Common triggers are an empty pan on high heat, a warped pan, or a blocked cooling vent beneath the cooktop.
symptoms: Fan audible for long after use

fixSteps.title: Let it cool
fixSteps.instruction: Remove pans and let the cooktop cool for 20 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clear vents
fixSteps.instruction: Make sure the intake under the cooktop and the exhaust at the back are not blocked.

fixSteps.title: Test fan
fixSteps.instruction: From the cabinet below, confirm the cooling fan runs when a zone is on.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the fan runs but zones still overheat; the coil temperature sensor may be at fault.

faq.a: Yes, only the overheated zone is disabled.

title: Incompatible or missing cookware
shortDescription: The induction zone does not detect a ferrous pan.
fullDescription:
E3 is specific to induction models and means the selected zone cannot find a compatible pan. The pan base must be magnetic and at least 12 cm in diameter.

Aluminum, copper, and some stainless pans will not work.
symptoms: Zone beeps and turns off after a few seconds

fixSteps.title: Magnet test
fixSteps.instruction: Stick a fridge magnet to the bottom of the pan. If it holds, the pan is compatible.

fixSteps.title: Match pan size
fixSteps.instruction: Use a pan whose base matches the zone diameter.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro only if E3 appears with a known-good pan on multiple zones.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch induction cooktop E3 pan error

faq.a: Only if the base is magnetic and flat.

title: Voltage supply fault
shortDescription: Line voltage is outside the operating range of the cooktop.
fullDescription:
E4 means the cooktop measured mains voltage too low or too high. Induction cooktops need a clean 208-240V, split-phase supply.

A loose neutral, a mis-wired outlet, or a brownout can all produce this error.

fixSteps.title: Reset breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the cooktop breaker off for 2 minutes and back on.

fixSteps.title: Have wiring checked
fixSteps.instruction: An electrician should measure each leg to neutral; each should read ~120V.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician if E4 persists after a breaker reset.

faq.a: Yes, surges often latch the cooktop into E4 until cycled.

title: Induction coil overheat
shortDescription: A coil temperature sensor reported the coil itself is overheating.
fullDescription:
E5 is a protective fault that shuts a zone down when the coil under the glass exceeds safe temperature. This often follows a blocked cooling fan or airflow restriction.

Persistent E5 codes mean the cooling system needs service.

fixSteps.title: Inspect under cabinet
fixSteps.instruction: Check for paper, plastic, or stored items under the cooktop blocking airflow.

fixSteps.title: Fan cleaning
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum the cooling fan intake; replace the fan if noisy.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the fan and intake look clean but E5 returns.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch cooktop E5 coil overheat fix

faq.a: The shutdown protects the electronics; just let it cool.

title: Communication loss between boards
shortDescription: Control and power boards cannot exchange data.
fullDescription:
E6 means the user interface and the induction power module are not communicating. On Bosch flex-induction units, the bridge bus between modules can fail or a connector may loosen after a repair.

The cooktop locks out all zones until communication restores.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Trip the breaker for 10 minutes and restore.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Access the underside and reseat every board-to-board connector.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if cables look fine and the fault persists.

faq.a: No, all zones lock out until the error clears.

title: Coil-to-pan coupling poor
shortDescription: The induction coil cannot couple efficiently with the pan placed on it.
fullDescription:
E7 is an efficiency fault. The induction zone is working but the coupling to the pan is poor, causing abnormal current draw. It usually means a warped pan or a pan that is slightly off-center.

Replace or recenter the pan; if the error persists across multiple pans, the zone's inverter may be failing.

fixSteps.title: Reposition pan
fixSteps.instruction: Center the pan on the zone markings.

fixSteps.title: Test with flat pan
fixSteps.instruction: Use a known flat-bottom induction pan to confirm.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro only if the error repeats with multiple good pans.

faq.a: Yes, very thin bases heat unevenly and can trigger E7.

title: Cooling fan speed fault
shortDescription: The cooling fan RPM is outside the expected range.
fullDescription:
E8 indicates the fan tachometer is reporting an RPM that is too low or too high. Debris in the fan, a failing motor bearing, or a disconnected sensor wire can all cause this.

The cooktop reduces power to protect itself until the fan is fixed.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum fan intake
fixSteps.instruction: From under the cabinet, vacuum lint and dust out of the fan.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the fan assembly if noise or fault continues.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the fan is new but E8 persists; the control may need replacement.

faq.q: Why does dust accumulate so fast?
faq.a: The fan pulls cabinet air up through the cooktop.

title: Child lock sensor stuck
shortDescription: The lock key reads as continuously pressed.
fullDescription:
E9 tells you the child-lock touch key is stuck, preventing normal operation. Liquid on the glass or a failed sensor can both cause it.

Cleaning the surface almost always clears it; persistent E9 means the touch module has failed.

fixSteps.title: Clean and dry
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the control strip with a dry microfiber cloth.

fixSteps.title: Replace touch module
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning fails, install a new touch control module.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if replacing the module does not clear the error.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch cooktop E9 child lock fix

faq.q: Is the child lock still active?
faq.a: Yes, the cooktop is locked until the fault clears.

title: General electronics fault
shortDescription: Internal self-test of the power electronics failed.
fullDescription:
F0 is a catch-all for power module faults that do not have their own code. A self-test at power-on failed, usually pointing to the induction generator board.

A full power cycle sometimes clears it, but recurring F0 means the power board needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Switch the breaker off for 15 minutes and back on.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Book a technician to test and replace the power module.

whenToCallPro: Always call a pro; HV capacitors and 240V wiring are inside.

faq.a: No, it locks out until cleared.

title: NTC sensor short circuit
shortDescription: A zone temperature sensor is reading a short.
fullDescription:
F1 means the NTC thermistor for one zone reads as shorted (near 0 ohms). The cooktop disables that zone to prevent runaway heating.

A crushed wire or a failed thermistor are the usual culprits.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Trip the breaker and retest.

fixSteps.title: Replace NTC
fixSteps.instruction: A technician should replace the NTC sensor for the affected coil.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro; sensor swap requires lifting the glass carefully.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch cooktop F1 sensor short fix

faq.a: Each zone has its own sensor and inverter.

title: NTC sensor open circuit
shortDescription: A zone temperature sensor is reading open.
fullDescription:
F2 is the opposite of F1: the NTC is reading infinite resistance. The control disables the zone because it cannot read its temperature.

A broken wire, disconnected plug, or failed thermistor are the common causes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connectors
fixSteps.instruction: From under the cabinet, reseat the NTC plug for the affected coil.

fixSteps.title: Replace NTC
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the sensor if reseating does not help.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro; accessing the coil means lifting the glass.
videoSearchQuery: Bosch cooktop F2 sensor open fix

faq.q: Can I keep cooking on other zones?
faq.a: Yes, only the faulted zone is locked out.
